verdict.headline: Nasdaq has its worst day since June on chip and Meta selling as the 10-year falls below 5%
verdict.label: Close: Nasdaq 26,008.86 (-2.60%), S&P 500 7,663.43 (-1.21%), Dow 52,867.98 (+0.02%), Russell 2000 2,784.03 (+0.11%); VIX 19.03; 10Y ~4.96% (about -17 bp); Brent $113.17 (+4%); chip index more than -6%, Lam Research -11.76%, Meta -6.98%, AMD -8.10%.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: the Nasdaq fell 2.60% to 26,008.86, its worst day since June, and the S&P 500 fell 1.21% to 7,663.43, its worst since July. The Dow ended up 0.02% and the Russell 2000 0.11%, and most US stocks rose. The chip index fell more than 6% after Lam Research said supply constraints would push some shipments from the December quarter into March; Lam fell 11.76%, AMD 8.1% and Nvidia 4.4%. Meta fell nearly 7% after lifting its 2026 expense range to $175-179 billion. The 10-year yield fell about 17 basis points to 4.96%, its largest one-day drop since March 2023, while Brent rose 4% to $113.17.

What it means: this morning's report said closes below 26,424.82 on the Nasdaq and 7,666.45 on the S&P 500 would show Wednesday's rebound failed, and both happened, the S&P 500 by only 3 points. The selling was concentrated in AI holdings, and the money went to Treasuries and the rest of the market, not to gold, which fell about 2.4%. Bonds weighed slower growth above oil-driven inflation for the day.

What would change the picture: a Nasdaq close back above 26,424.82 by the October 28 Fed decision would show this was a one-day reaction to two results. A 10-year back above Wednesday's 5.11% would show the bond buying was a one-day refuge. Microsoft's and Alphabet's results on October 28 are the next test of AI spending.
verdict.lede_short: The Nasdaq fell 2.6%, its worst day since June, as Lam Research's supply warning sent chips down more than 6% and Meta's higher expense range cost it nearly 7%, while most other US stocks rose. Bond buyers took the other side, pulling the 10-year about 17 basis points to 4.96% even as Brent rose 4%. A Nasdaq close back above 26,424.82 would mean today's break did not hold.

supporting_data.label: The Nasdaq fell 2.6% and the S&P 500 1.2% for its worst day since July, while most US stocks rose — the loss came from the largest AI holdings, not from a broad retreat from stocks.

The chip index fell more than 6% after Lam Research cited supply chain constraints, with Lam down 11.76%, AMD 8.1% and Nvidia 4.4% — the market read a supplier shortage as a cap on how fast AI chip sales can grow next quarter.

Meta lifted its 2026 total expense range to $175-179 billion after a quarter with free cash flow of about -$2.1 billion — Wednesday's after-hours gain reversed into a near-7% fall once costs were weighed against the revenue beat.

The 10-year yield fell about 17 basis points to 4.96%, its largest one-day drop since March 2023, as the VIX rose 14% to 19.03 — Treasuries acted as the refuge from the tech selling and broke the 5.0% line.

Brent rose 4% to $113.17, its highest close since May 4, on reports the US plans to resume strikes on Iran — oil and yields moved in opposite directions, so bonds weighed slower growth above oil-driven inflation.
Jobless claims fell to 194,000 against 200,000 expected — the bond rally did not come from labour data but from investors leaving tech.

trade_setups.thesis: Both indexes closed below the levels that defined Wednesday's rebound, the S&P 500 by only 3 points, on selling concentrated in chips and Meta while most stocks rose.
trade_setups.entry: Nasdaq 26,424.82 and S&P 500 7,666.45 above; Thursday's 26,008.86 and 7,663.43 closes.
trade_setups.invalidation: Closes back above both by the October 28 Fed decision would show a one-day reaction to two results; a second lower close led by chips would show the funding and supply questions setting prices.
trade_setups.horizon: Through Microsoft's and Alphabet's results on October 28

trade_setups.invalidation: A 10-year back above 5.11% would show the bond buying was a one-day refuge; resumed US strikes on Iran would test the pattern.
